key_claims: A subset of neurons in the dorsal dentate gyrus of aged mice accumulates H3K9me3 via the methyltransferase Suv39h1.
H3K9me3 high neurons express a transcriptional state that fails to induce plasticity machinery while engaging memory-stabilization programs.
H3K9me3 accumulation interferes with neuronal activation and synaptic remodeling in response to behavioral stimulation in aged mice.
Genetically inhibiting Suv39h1 to lower dDG-H3K9me3 high numbers improved memory in aged mice.
limitations: The findings are based on a study of aged mice rather than humans.
Surrogate or biomarker-based measurements do not measure tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
what_not_to_say: Do not claim that these findings demonstrate human clinical efficacy or provide medical guidance.
Do not state that surrogate or epigenetic clock scores measure tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
